reason: E4 supports the feasibility of using DFT with ML force fields and Green-Kubo for lattice conductivity, and E3 supports the premise that force-constant disorder is a dominant phonon scattering source. However, no cited evidence supports the specific quantitative predictions of equal contributions below 200 K or the 10–17 W/(K m) range, nor does any cited work demonstrate successful independent computation of electronic transport in this alloy.
premises: DFT can independently compute electronic transport properties (plasma frequency, effective mass, relaxation times) for HfNbTaTiZr.
ML-trained force fields can capture phonon dynamics and lattice heat transport under realistic oxygen-contaminated conditions.
Force-constant disorder and oxygen-induced defects are the dominant phonon scattering sources in HfNbTaTiZr.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic contributions to thermal conductivity are approximately equal.
At 300–1200 K, total thermal conductivity for ~1 wt% oxygen samples is 10–17 W/(K m).
